summary:
Source candidate for #5170 implements the November 3 user supersession: trigger on at least 200 active Done cards, rank closed readable cards by closedAt then repository/number/item identity, retain the newest 50, then apply older live-blocker protection. Protected rows inside the newest 50 count toward retention. Open/unrankable Done or older protected rows prevent exact retention and scheduled complete-cycle mode refuses before writes. This source finding does not assert current deployed policy or permission for archive writes.

The scheduled adapter pins keep50, triggerAt200 and completeCycle in the accepted receipt. It requires the entire plan to fit its per-run cap before writes, archives oldest first, and clears its existing durable cross-run latch only for a validated complete journal: planned equals explicit activeDone minus50, every intent has its matching archive readback, no skips or unknowns. A bounded prefix or underdeclared plan cannot settle, even after partial effects leave fewer than200Done. Root reads original custody/native effects and selects continuation; there is no automatic resend or latch clearing. Legacy keep200 receipts remain history and cannot activate changed source.

The unchanged500-item scan bound permits at most450candidates, conservatively1360API calls and902successful custody records. The child has an independent1800-second deadline inside1860-second service runtime; slow/failing work retains custody and its latch rather than promising completion. F# tend now mirrors the pure Python candidate planner for write exclusion: inclusive activeDone200, default retention50, the same closeTime/repository/numeric-number/item ranking and post-cutoff native blocker protection. Incomplete live blocker lists refuse eligibility. Acquisition preserves PR Done/state/closeTime and unreadable-card Status; unknown issue state is not treated as closed. It adds no F# archive sender or schema field. Paired Python/F# fixed fixtures cover the same tied identities and protection cutoff; focused guard mutants expose off-by-one trigger, wrong retention, missing protection and missing repository ranking. Protected CI, publication/installed adoption, accepted live execution, new activation and scheduled readback remain separate acceptance work. Native blocker relationships must be refreshed before any real cycle; this record is not their live truth.

Below the trigger, the pure planner returns no archive candidates and retains every rankable Done row. The printed "keep newest N" is the actual retained count, not the configured keep50 parameter: N can exceed50 below200. A natural scheduled no-op is valid schedule-path evidence when the actual permanent timer LastTrigger joins one service invocation, complete before/after native preservation, source/config/reader pins, settled completion and absent unresolved latch. It is distinct from a prior manual validation and from a prior nonzero drain. A brief live latch need not have been sampled: disclose that limit and join the exact maintained settlement/unlink source to actual completion. Preserve failed/partial observation originals; an offline parser correction must not restart the service, replace original effects or renew the original observation deadline. Public Root schedule acceptance is https://github.com/FS-GG/.github/issues/5170#issuecomment-6622854128; this record stores the reusable boundary, not changing board counts or runtime assets. A new schedule no-op cannot settle an unresolved older drain.
title: Done retention separates inclusive trigger from fifty-card retention and settles a complete bounded cycle
